## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One issue needs fixing: `requirement_proven` has lost its empty-input guard. Because of that, a requirement with no criteria is now reported as proven. This review found no other defects in the two changed files, both of which were read in full.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/proof.py:3 — correctness — `requirement_proven([])` now returns `True`, but the base version returned `False`. With no criteria, `sum(...)` is `0` and `len(criteria)` is `0`, so `proven == len(criteria)` holds. The old code `bool(criteria) and all(...)` deliberately rejected this case. To fix it, restore the guard, for example `return bool(criteria) and proven == len(criteria)` (or keep the original `all(...)` form), and add `assert not requirement_proven([])` to `test_requirement_with_evidence` in tests/test_proof.py:6. No test currently covers empty input. — Any requirement with no evidence attached is reported as proven, so status summaries show unproven requirements as satisfied, and no test would catch the regression.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `reviewed_batch` rejects an empty batch with a clear `ValueError` message. tests/test_proof.py:11-17 covers the empty, all-reviewed and mixed cases.
